# H054 — The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals.

**Step:** [step-8](../README.md) — Is mosaic aneuploidy detectable in the sequenced sample with a statistic that has power, and what cell-fraction bound does the data set per chromosome?
**Status:** supported  |  **Confidence:** 0.85  |  **Revisions:** 2
**Gene:** —  |  **Path:** mosaic

## The claim

The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals.

**Prediction if true.** For each chromosome, the dosage bootstrap interval and the allele-balance fraction estimate interval overlap, or both are consistent with no event.

**What would refute it.** A chromosome where the two intervals do not overlap -- the step then names which instrument is wrong and why, rather than averaging them.

| 142 | supports | 0.75 | measurement | The dosage route recovers one copy of X at 0.4873 and one copy of Y at 0.5083 against an expected 0.5, on the two chromosomes where the allele-balance route has no heterozygous sites to read, so the two instruments are complementary rather than redundant. | `docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/121-the-second-instrument-and-the-shards-it-did-not-need.md` |
| 143 | neutral | 0.50 | measurement | chr21 mean depth at called sites is 61.68x against a 42.42x baseline but its median is 45 against 43 and its 99th percentile 247 against 66 to 69 on clean autosomes, so the depth excess is a tail of mismapping pileups among the acrocentric chromosomes and not copy number. | `docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/121-the-second-instrument-and-the-shards-it-did-not-need.md` |
| 144 | supports | 0.30 | measurement | The absolute k-mer-mass denominator (calibration-set mean) and the autosomal-median denominator agree on all 24 contigs to within 0.017 percent (ratio 1.02767 to 1.02784), so the median assumption distorted no chromosome in this sample; defence (c) of the plan is measured, not assumed. | `methodology/123` |

## Weighing

```
prior 0.50  (log-odds +0.000)
  +1.600  supports 0.80 — k-mer dosage over 32 flowcell shards puts no autosome beyond its composition-corrected null after multiple testing: the largest residual is chr21 at 2.33 sigma, Bonferroni p 0.43 across 22 autosomes, and it falls to 1.60 sigma when 10 percent is trimmed from each tail.   -> 0.832
  +1.500  supports 0.75 — The dosage route recovers one copy of X at 0.4873 and one copy of Y at 0.5083 against an expected 0.5, on the two chromosomes where the allele-balance route has no heterozygous sites to read, so the two instruments are complementary rather than redundant.   -> 0.957
  +0.000  neutral 0.50 — chr21 mean depth at called sites is 61.68x against a 42.42x baseline but its median is 45 against 43 and its 99th percentile 247 against 66 to 69 on clean autosomes, so the depth excess is a tail of mismapping pileups among the acrocentric chromosomes and not copy number.   -> 0.957
  +0.600  supports 0.30 — The absolute k-mer-mass denominator (calibration-set mean) and the autosomal-median denominator agree on all 24 contigs to within 0.017 percent (ratio 1.02767 to 1.02784), so the median assumption distorted no chromosome in this sample; defence (c) of the plan is measured, not assumed.   -> 0.976
suggested confidence 0.98 (3 supporting, 0 refuting, 1 neutral)
```

The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior: the strengths are human judgments, and rows drawn from the same underlying data are not independent the way the sum treats them.

## History

| Rev | Status | Confidence | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | proposed | — | — |
| 2 | supported | 0.85 | Both routes report no event where both can see, and they share nothing past the FASTQ: allele balance puts no chromosome above its 2-3 percent detection limit, and k-mer dosage puts none beyond its composition-corrected null (largest chr21, Bonferroni p 0.43, falling to 1.60 sigma when trimmed). Where only dosage can see it recovers one copy of X (0.4873) and Y (0.5083) against an expected 0.5. Held below the suggested 0.96 for two reasons stated rather than hidden: the two supporting rows come from the same single pass and the weighing treats them as independent when they are not; and the test itself was changed after pre-registration, because the bootstrap interval the claim named measures counting noise rather than the composition bias that dominates this measurement, so the comparison was made against the residual spread instead. The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior. |
